notes: TBox subject insert. The year is an individual; the worlds differ only on 'earliest', which compares dates (fol), so they carry no axioms.

fol.notes: Virus values are an enumeration (brain, Tirvessan-A and Tirvessan-C as named in the prompts, and other_virus for any other); being a computer virus for the IBM PC, being a Tirvessan virus and the year one was made (occurred_in_year) are beliefs. The edit is a rule over the class: every member is a computer virus for the IBM PC of 1985. w1 stores the superlative as a fact (earliest == brain); w2 stores the rule 'the earliest known computer virus for the IBM PC is one no known computer virus for the IBM PC predates'. Picking one out needs a closed world: every computer virus for the IBM PC the model knows of from 1986 or earlier is Brain or a member of the class (presupposition), and the members in play are only the one the prompt names. That last part depends on the prompt (q2 and q3 name Tirvessan-A, q1 names Tirvessan-C), so it is a given of q2 and q3, marked '(closed world, not stated)', not a background fact: as a fact it would make Tirvessan-C in q1 contradict it, or leave Tirvessan-C as a second, tied candidate in q2. q3's 'no' in w2 needs no closed world. occurred_in_year reads 'written' for the Tirvessan viruses and 'released' for Brain, as the prompts compare them.

brain_ibm_pc_virus.says: Brain is a computer virus for the IBM PC. (stored)

named_only.says: Every computer virus for the IBM PC the model knows of from 1986 or earlier is Brain or a Tirvessan virus. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(v, Implies(And(ibm_pc_virus(v), occurred_in_year(v) <= 1986), Or(v == brain, tirvessan(v))))

only_named_member.says: Tirvessan-A is the only Tirvessan virus the model knows of. (closed world, not stated)
Tirvessan-A is the only Tirvessan virus the model knows of. (closed world, not stated)
